answer: An agent economy can make each identity carry a crystal-clear, verifiable history: every completed job is signed and stored in a public grove of records that anyone can audit. A newcomer starts with no reputation and earns trust only through small, attested tasks before touching anything valuable, while raven-like observers flag accounts appearing in flocks with identical behaviour. A sybil attacker must therefore build a separate credible history for every fake identity, paying real work and time for each one, so forging a thousand identities costs a thousand times the effort.
